t: A coalition of the ulama, liberal and radical intellectuals and the bazaar forced the Qajar shah to accept a parliament in 1906, though the three groups were united by common enemies rather than common goals.
Clerics were on both sides: Akhund Khurasani and two other leading marja' in Najaf backed the constitution, while Fazlollah Nouri opposed it and was hanged in July 1909.
Constitutionalists restored the constitution in 1909 after the Minor Tyranny, but the revolution ended in December 1911 when the Second Majlis was expelled with the support of 12,000 Russian troops.
dyk: The tobacco protest of 1891 to 1892 worked so well that Iranians stopped smoking despite their love of tobacco, and it was said that even the women of the shah's harem gave it up.
ev: The tobacco protest begins against a 50-year monopoly granted to an Englishman, and Mirza Hasan Shirazi's fatwa of December 1891 closes the bazaars and stops the smoking of tobacco
Merchants and clergy protest against tariffs imposed to repay the Russian loan for the shah's tour of Europe
Mozaffar ad-Din Shah agrees to a parliament, and the National Consultative Assembly first meets in October
The Anglo-Russian Convention divides Iran into a Russian zone in the north and a British zone in the south
Mohammad Ali Shah stages a coup and bombards the parliament, beginning the Minor Tyranny
Constitutionalist forces march on Tehran, force the shah to abdicate and re-establish the constitution; Fazlollah Nouri is hanged in July
Sattar Khan refuses to disarm and is wounded in a confrontation with Yeprem Khan, the police chief of Tehran
In December the shah's cabinet, backed by 12,000 Russian troops, expels the deputies of the Second Majlis

f.where: Iran (Persia): Tehran, Tabriz, Rasht, Qazvin, Isfahan and other cities, with the Shi'i schools of Najaf in Iraq giving rulings from outside.
f.period: Protest against the customs director and the shah's loans (1905); the shah's agreement to a house of justice (January 1906) and to a parliament (August 1906); the first Majlis (from October 1906); the Minor Tyranny and civil war (1908–1909); the second constitutional period (1909–1911); the expulsion of the deputies of the Second Majlis (December 1911).
f.figures: Mozaffar ad-Din Shah Qajar and Mohammad Ali Shah Qajar; the clerics Akhund Khurasani, Mirza Husayn Tehrani, Shaykh Abdullah Mazandarani, Sayyed Mohammad Tabatabai and Fazlollah Nouri; the Tabriz commanders Sattar Khan and Bagher Khan; Yeprem Khan; the American lawyer William Morgan Shuster.
f.outcome: A parliament with final approval of loans and the budget, and a constitution that lasted, though not adhered to, until 1979; but also the Anglo-Russian division of the country in 1907, the shelling of the Majlis in 1908, and the expulsion of the Second Majlis in 1911 with the support of 12,000 Russian troops.
